text:
vivek: Quick discovery while updating our sample-apps: a docker-compose quickstart uses a .env example that sets REDWOOD_KEY instead of REDWOOD_API_KEY and the ruby + csharp samples read different env names. New hire ran `docker-compose up` and the container started but all requests returned 401.

izzy: Oof. Where is that file?

vivek: In `examples/todo/README.md` and the repo root `.env.example`. Snippet that tripped them:

```
# .env.example (bad)
REDWOOD_KEY=sk-REDACTED
DOCKER_HOST=0.0.0.0
```

And docker-compose.yml mounts .env so users copy/paste and think it's configured. The app code (Ruby) expects ENV['REDWOOD_API_KEY']. The C# sample in `examples/clients/csharp/README.md` uses a property `options.ApiKey = ...` instead of `options.Token = ...` so it bypasses our token rotation helper.

marco: Nice find. That explains the 401 flow. Also saw the docker-compose healthcheck curl example missing Content-Type and using `Token:` header.

izzy: Can you paste the problematic C# snippet?

vivek: Sure:

```csharp
// bad
var options = new RedwoodOptions();
options.ApiKey = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("REDWOOD_API_KEY");
var client = new RedwoodClient(options);
```

Correct approach (uses token property so SDK hooks run):

```csharp
// good
var options = new RedwoodOptions();
options.Token = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("REDWOOD_API_KEY");
var client = new RedwoodClient(options);
```

The difference is subtle but important: setting ApiKey circumvents the built-in retry/session wiring and KMS rotations.

izzy: We should unify .env.example and update every README to reference REDWOOD_API_KEY only, and avoid showing any `sk-` literal. Also update docker quickstart to explicitly mention not to commit .env and to use Docker secrets in prod.

marco: Also saw a Node example inside sample-app that does `await fetch(url)` without `keepalive` or connection pooling; with heavy local testing that caused sockets to pile up. We should show recommended Node http.Agent reuse or use the SDK client which manages keepalive. Tiny note in the quickstart: "Prefer SDK client reuse over raw fetch per request."

vivek: I'll open a docs PR to:
- Replace REDWOOD_KEY with REDWOOD_API_KEY in .env.example and all READMEs
- Replace any `Token:` or `X-Api-Key` headers in curl healthchecks with `Authorization: Bearer` and include Content-Type
- Update C# sample to use options.Token and add a short comment about rotation/retry
- Add a short Docker gotcha: do not commit .env, prefer Docker secrets, and confirm env var names
- Fix Node sample to show Agent reuse or recommend SDK


docs-bot: Reminder: docs PRs that change examples must include runnable snippets where possible and a changelog entry. Also please run the docs grep for `REDWOOD_KEY`, `X-Api-Key`, and `sk-` literals.

izzy: Can we add a quick docs CI check that fails the build if `.env.example` contains deprecated keys or if any README codeblock has `sk-` or `REDWOOD_KEY`? I can add a small grep job.

ci-bot: I will add a docs CI job that scans repo for regexes: `\bREDWOOD_KEY\b`, `\bX-Api-Key\b`, and `\bsk-[A-Za-z0-9]+\b` inside fenced code blocks and fail if found. Also add a checklist item to the PR template to run `make docs-lint`.

marco: Filed issue #4780 to track the sweep + CI rule. Assigning @vivek for the PR and @izzy for CI changes.

vivek: Opening PR now titled "docs: unify env var, fix docker-compose & SDK samples". Will tag @marco and @izzy for review. Thanks all — small fixes but should cut onboarding confusion a lot. :seedling:
